name: tlqa
instructions: Treat TimeLogic TLQA as temporal-logic verification over localized video events.
For every referenced action, retrieve or open evidence until you can assign a timestamp interval.
Represent each action as start-end seconds before applying before, after, overlap, imply, always, or immediately operators.

First classify the question into one TLQA operator family: eventual, always, until, since, disjoint, imply, before, after, co-occur, immediate-next, always-before, always-after, always-co-occur, strict-chain, loose-chain, or one-before-two.
Eventual pattern: `Does the person eventually X?` requires at least one localized X interval.
Always pattern: `Is the person always X?` requires X to hold throughout the checked video span.
Until pattern: `Did the person X until Y?` requires X to continue before Y happens.
Since pattern: `Has the person been X since they Y?` requires Y earlier and X after Y.
Disjoint pattern: `X does not overlap with Y` requires no overlap between X and Y intervals.
Implies pattern: `Does X imply Y?` requires each visible X occurrence to have supporting Y.
Before pattern: `Did X before Y?` requires a localized X interval before Y.
After/Next pattern: `Did X after Y?` is evaluated as Y before X.
Co-occur pattern: `Do X and Y co-occur?` requires overlapping X and Y intervals.
Immediate-next pattern: `Did X immediately after Y?` requires X right after Y with no unrelated gap.
Always-before pattern: `Did X always before Y?` requires every Y to be preceded by X.
Always-after pattern: `Did X always after Y?` requires every Y to be followed by X.
Always-co-occur pattern: `Does X always co-occur with Y?` requires every X occurrence to overlap Y.
Strict-chain pattern: `A always before B, which always before C` requires strict repeated A -> B -> C ordering.
Loose-chain pattern: `A before B, which before C` requires at least one A -> B -> C ordering.
One-before-two pattern: `A always before B and C` requires A before both B and C.
For multiple-choice questions, evaluate the temporal formula independently for every option and choose the option whose interval relation satisfies the formula.
For boolean questions, map option A to yes and option B to no, then answer only yes or no after the final option-letter step.
If all operator-required events are localized and exactly one option or boolean verdict is symbolically verified, stop immediately with that option letter.
Do not choose from semantic similarity alone; verify the symbolic temporal relation against the event intervals.
